Listen to this article Share Dangote Petroleum Refinery is set to increase its initial public offering (IPO) size by up to 30 percent to about $2.1 billion after attracting investor subscriptions worth nearly N6 trillion, or about $4.5 billion, in one of Nigeria’s biggest equity fundraising exercises. Advertisement Advertisement Reuters, in a report on Tuesday, disclosed that the proposed expansion follows strong demand for the refinery’s shares, with investors placing orders worth nearly three times the initial offer, prompting the company to consider exercising its overallotment option to accommodate additional subscriptions. Three people involved in the transaction and a senior company executive disclosed the development, according to a Reuters report on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The refinery initially planned to offer 4.1 billion shares to investors but is now expected to allot as many as 5.33 billion shares, including an overallotment option, one of the lead advisers to the transaction said. The enlarged offering, if completed, would rank among the largest stock market listings in Africa, reflecting growing investor appetite for exposure to Nigeria’s industrial and energy sectors. A senior Dangote executive said the refinery intended to issue additional shares up to the permitted regulatory limit, with the final details subject to approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Advertisement The company is expected to list on the Nigerian Exchange later this month, marking a significant step in its plans to broaden ownership and deepen its access to the domestic capital market. The allocation structure suggests that retail investors will receive all the shares they applied for, while domestic pension funds are expected to secure allocations close to their subscription requests. Advertisement Foreign investors, however, are likely to bear the bulk of the scaling back as the company seeks to accommodate demand within the expanded offer. Read also: BoI boosts Abia SMEs with ₦1.041bn funding Advertisement Advertisement “The guys that won’t get all their allotment are the offshore guys,” one of the advisers involved in the transaction said. A stockbroker working on the offering said additional shares would be allocated on a pro-rata basis to investors who subscribed for more than 100 million shares. Demand from outside Nigeria was particularly strong across African markets, with investors from South Africa, Botswana and Kenya leading subscriptions. South Africa’s Public Investment Corporation was also among the institutional investors that participated in the offer, the adviser said. The strong response highlights the refinery’s appeal beyond Nigeria, as investors seek exposure to one of Africa’s largest industrial infrastructure projects and its potential role in transforming the continent’s petroleum products market. Built by Africa’s richest man, Aliko Dangote, the refinery has become a major component of Nigeria’s strategy to reduce dependence on imported petroleum products, strengthen domestic refining capacity and improve energy security. Beyond the public offering, the refinery had already raised approximately $2.5 billion through two private placements involving 7.2 billion shares, according to its IPO prospectus. The prospectus, however, did not disclose the identities of the investors who participated in the private placements. The IPO is not underwritten, although Pan-African Refinery Investment SPV has committed to subscribe for up to $400 million, representing approximately 19 percent of the enlarged offering. The amount ultimately allocated to the investment vehicle was not immediately clear. Following the public offering, Dangote is expected to retain approximately 83.5 percent ownership of the refinery, while the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC), an early investor in the project, is expected to see its stake decline to about 6.5 percent. “The anticipated reduction in NNPC’s ownership reflects the dilution arising from the enlarged share offering, although Dangote will retain overwhelming control of the business after its listing,” the report disclosed.
